title: Comparison of three different ELISAs for the detection of recombinant, native and plasma IL-17A
author: Ismail, Åkefeldt, et al.

steps.title: Coat plate with capture antibody
steps.instruction: Dilute capture antibodies 500-P07G, 41802 and eBio64CAP17 in PBS‑1X to final concentrations of 0.5 µg/mL and 4 µg/mL, respectively; add 100 µL of each diluted antibody to each well, cover the ELISA plate and incubate overnight at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash plate after coating
steps.instruction: Aspirate the liquid from each well and wash the plate four times with 250 µL washing buffer per well; after the final wash invert the plate to remove residual buffer and blot on a paper towel.

steps.title: Block non‑specific binding
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL blocking buffer to each well, cover the plate and incubate for at least 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash plate after blocking
steps.instruction: Aspirate the blocking buffer and wash the plate four times as described in step 2.

steps.title: Add standards and samples
steps.instruction: Dilute the recombinant human IL‑17A standard from 2 ng/mL down to zero in dilution buffer; add 100 µL of each standard dilution or sample to the appropriate wells in duplicate and cover the plate.

steps.title: Incubate samples
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature for at least 2 h.

steps.title: Wash plate after sample incubation
steps.instruction: Aspirate the sample solution and wash the plate four times as described in step 2.

steps.title: Add biotinylated detection antibody
steps.instruction: Dilute biotinylated 500-P07G antibody in dilution buffer to a final concentration of 0.25 µg/mL; add 100 µL per well and cover the plate.

steps.title: Incubate detection antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature for 2 h.

steps.title: Wash plate after detection antibody
steps.instruction: Aspirate the detection antibody solution and wash the plate four times as described in step 2.

steps.title: Add avidin‑HRP conjugate
steps.instruction: Dilute avidin‑HRP 1:2000 in dilution buffer; add 100 µL per well and cover the plate.

steps.title: Incubate avidin‑HRP
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate for 30 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Wash plate and remove bubbles
steps.instruction: Aspirate the avidin‑HRP solution and wash the plate four times as described in step 2; then aspirate any remaining bubbles from the wells.

steps.title: Add ABTS substrate
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of ABTS substrate solution (pre‑equilibrated to room temperature) to each well, avoiding bubble formation, and cover the plate.

steps.title: Develop color in dark
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature in the dark to allow color development.

steps.title: Read absorbance and record OD
steps.instruction: Read the plate with an ELISA plate reader at 405 nm (with wavelength correction set at 650 nm) at five‑minute intervals for 15 min; ensure the optical density does not exceed 1.2 or 1.4 depending on the batch.

steps.title: Generate standard curve and calculate concentrations
steps.instruction: Plot a standard curve using grade‑4 polynomial regression; interpolate sample OD values to determine IL‑17A concentrations.

steps.title: Note limits of detection
steps.instruction: Record the limits of detection for each ELISA: 10 pg/mL for E_500‑P07G, 13 pg/mL for E_41802, and 23 pg/mL for E_eBio64CAP17.
